objective: Write tests/test_audit_bus.py that drive make_audit_consumer through a real Bus — publish on 'audit' creates exactly one audit row and a redelivered copy of the same event (same ts, actor, action) creates no second row — and extend ledger/worker.py only if a new test fails against the current consumer, preserving the (ts, actor, action) dedup key.

concepts: dedup via store.find before insert on (ts, actor, action)
bus-level redelivery as a test scenario (publish the same event twice)

non_goals: tests/test_ledger.py (owned by T01 — read as a style reference only)
changing the dedup key or the make_audit_consumer(store) signature (C4)
implementation_constraints: stdlib only; unittest style matching tests/test_ledger.py
test events are hand-built from the C1 spec (exact key set) — do not import or call handle_transfer in this module
ledger/worker.py changes are allowed only to make a failing new test pass, and must preserve C4 exactly (signature, dedup key, return shapes)

deliverables.what: worker.py unchanged, or a minimal C4-preserving extension

acceptance_tests.description: publishing a well-formed C1 event on 'audit' via the bus creates exactly 1 audit row whose fields equal the event fields; the consume result is {'ok': True, 'deduped': False}
publishing a copy of the same event (same ts, actor, action) via the bus creates no second row; the consume result is {'ok': True, 'deduped': True} and the table length stays 1

failure_cases.scenario: a redelivered event arrives after the first insert (simulated by a second bus.publish of the same dict)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: consume's find() hits the existing row, the insert is skipped, and the table holds exactly 1 row for that (ts, actor, action)

handoff.notes: T04 re-runs the redelivery scenario as gate E3 end-to-end with the real publisher. If worker.py needed a change, the checkpoint records it with the failing test that forced it.
